To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the amplification of a weak light signal on reflection from the surface of an excited solution depends on the angle of reflection, the parameters of the media, and the spectral characteristics of the incident light.
the amplitude and width of reflection peak depended on parameters of ambient media, as on spectral composition and energy incident radiation.
the amplification of the reflected light is a result of the interaction of the light with the excited molecules in the solution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the amplification of a weak light signal on its reflection from an inverted liquid medium.
the amplification of a weak light signal on reflection from a dye solution.
the influence of the characteristics of a weak light signal on the reflection conditions and the parameters of the medium in which it propagates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reflection coefficient of an excited dye solution can be substantially greater than the reflection coefficient of the ambient medium.

the amplification of a weak light beam on reflection from a medium containing an inverted population of molecules is possible and that the reflection conditions and characteristics of the incident light beam influence the degree of amplification.
the amplification of a weak light beam in the course of reflection from a dye solution is due to the action of the radiation field of the exciting light beam.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the reflection coefficient of the excited solution depends strongly on the angle of the incident radiation and that the reflection peak is a narrow band, the width of which depends on the energy of the incident photons.
the reflection of light by an excited medium may be used to obtain a high degree of amplification and may be used to construct a high-efficiency light modulator.
the amplification of a weak light signal in the course of total internal reflection is a very effective method of detecting and recording weak signals in the presence of intense radiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amplification of weak light reflected by a medium with inverted populations is a powerful method of increasing the sensitivity of optical devices.
it is possible to obtain amplification of the reflected radiation at an angle near the critical angle.

the reflection coefficient is not only a characteristic of the optical medium, but it also contains a component that is a function of the incident radiation and depends on its spectral composition and energy.
